## Fault Localization Diagnostic Prompt

You are a debugging assistant specialized in Fault Localization. Your goal is to evaluate past issue reports to provide "Regional Context" and "Mechanism Context" for an agent exploring a codebase to find a root cause.

### Task

Evaluate each past report independently. Determine its diagnostic utility for localizing the current failure based on the provided test snippet and current bug report.

### Labels & Scoring Brackets

  * R (Relevant) [0.80 - 1.00] — Direct Functional Overlap:
    The reports share a root cause, faulty mechanism, or fix pattern. Use this when the past issue likely points to the same faulty method or logic block.

  * P (Partially Relevant) [0.30 - 0.79] — Contextual Utility:
    The report offers indirect clues for the localization process. This includes:

      * Regional Context: Shared package or subsystem proximity. Even if the logic differs, the report helps "warm up" the correct area of the codebase.
      * Mechanism Context: Shared technical sub-tasks that appear across different modules.
      * Heuristic: If the link is primarily structural with an unrelated mechanism, land at the lower end (0.30 - 0.39) to reflect a "neighborhood signal."

  * I (Irrelevant) [0.00 - 0.29] — Architectural Distance:
    Use this when reports share neither a structural neighborhood nor a functional pattern. A report is Irrelevant if it is in a different subsystem and addresses a fundamentally different logic type (e.g., File I/O vs. Numeric Parsing), providing zero diagnostic signal for the current failure.

### Output Format

For each report:
RPT\#[Issue\_Key]: \<R|P|I\> (\<score\>)
Reasoning: Briefly justify the evaluation by weighing the Regional Signal against the Functional Mechanism. Identify any shared data types or domains that influenced the judgment.

The test
['org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.model.ExternalXMLNamespaceTest.testElementDOM()']
failed.

The test looks like: 
    public void testElementDOM() {
        doTestElement(DocumentContainer.MODEL_DOM);
    }

Current bug report: 
{
    "summary": "Incomplete handling of undefined namespaces"
    "description": "Mcduffey, Joe <jdmcduf@nsa.gov>
Can someone tell me how to register namespaces so that attributes with namespaces does not cause the exception
org.apache.common.ri.model.dom.DOMNodePointer.createAttribute  
unknown namespace prefix: xsi
For example the following  
<ElementA A:myAttr="Mytype">  
 <B:ElementB>MY VALUE</B:ElementB>  
</ElementA>
Would result in the following exception:  
org.apache.common.ri.model.dom.DOMNodePointer.createAttribute  
unknown namespace prefix: A
FYI: In this example there was a namespace decaration in the file and I also manually called the  
registerNamespace(A,"/http...");  
registerNamespace(B,"/http...");
There was no problem encountered for elements. Only attributes. Can someone help? Thanks.
"
}

Recent bug reports: 
RPT#JXPATH-88: {
 "summary": "Add getPrefix(String namespaceURI) to JXPathContext"
 "description": "There is function getNamespaceURI(String prefix), but there is no inverted one. Need this in following case:
* reading XML
* check, if prefix for particular namespace is defined (using getPrefix)
* if defined - using prefix, specified in XML
* if not defined - define prefix and using it
Usual way - to define prefix always - is not good, since prefix can already be used in XML file with another namespace."
}

RPT#JXPATH-85: {
 "summary": "Restore binary compatibility with JXPath 1.2"
 "description": "I ran a CLIRR report comparing JXPath 1.2 with the current trunk and it higlighted one issue between the versions:
ERROR: 7004: org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.NamespaceResolver: In method 'public NamespaceResolver()' the number of arguments has changed
Looking at the source NamespaceResolver no longer has a no-parameter constructor - adding this back in would make the upcoming JXPath 1.3 version binary compatible with JXPath 1.2."
}

RPT#JXPATH-89: {
 "summary": "Cannot compare pointers that do not belong to the same tree"
 "description": "For XPath "$var | /MAIN/A" exception is thrown:
org.apache.commons.jxpath.JXPathException: Cannot compare pointers that do not belong to the same tree: '$var' and ''  
 at org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.model.NodePointer.compareNodePointers(NodePointer.java:665)  
 at org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.model.NodePointer.compareNodePointers(NodePointer.java:649)  
 at org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.model.NodePointer.compareNodePointers(NodePointer.java:649)  
 at org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.model.NodePointer.compareTo(NodePointer.java:639)  
 at java.util.Arrays.mergeSort(Arrays.java:1152)  
 at java.util.Arrays.sort(Arrays.java:1079)  
 at java.util.Collections.sort(Collections.java:113)  
 at org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.EvalContext.constructIterator(EvalContext.java:176)  
 at org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.EvalContext.hasNext(EvalContext.java:100)  
 at org.apache.commons.jxpath.JXPathContext.selectNodes(JXPathContext.java:648)  
 at org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.model.VariablePointerTestCase.testUnionOfVariableAndNode(VariablePointerTestCase.java:76)"
}

RPT#JXPATH-88: P (0.52)  
Reasoning: This is in the same namespace-handling area of JXPath and deals with prefix/namespace resolution, which is relevant to the current “unknown namespace prefix” failure. However, it focuses on adding `getPrefix(namespaceURI)` for choosing prefixes during XML reading, not on DOM attribute creation or undefined namespace handling in `DOMNodePointer.createAttribute`. So it provides useful regional/mechanism context, but not a direct match.

RPT#JXPATH-85: I (0.12)  
Reasoning: This is about binary compatibility and constructor signatures in `NamespaceResolver`, which is a different concern from runtime namespace resolution failures in DOM attribute processing. It shares only a very broad namespace-related class name, with no meaningful diagnostic overlap.

RPT#JXPATH-89: I (0.08)  
Reasoning: This report concerns pointer comparison and tree membership during XPath union sorting, which is unrelated to namespace prefix registration or DOM attribute creation. It is in the same library, but a different subsystem and mechanism, so it offers little localization value for the current failure.
